title: Open WebUI SafePlaywrightURLLoader -- T1190 redirect-following bypasses initial-URL-only SSRF validation
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54018 (GHSA-jrfp-m64g-pcwv,
CVSS 7.7 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

`SafePlaywrightURLLoader` implements `validate_url` to block SSRF by
checking the IP address a submitted URL resolves to -- but this check
runs ONLY on the initial URL. Playwright follows HTTP redirects
(301/302) automatically by default, so a submitted URL that is itself
safe -- and passes validation -- can redirect to a restricted internal
address (localhost, a Docker container's internal network, or cloud
metadata) that the loader then fetches without re-validating. This
reaches internal services even when `ENABLE_RAG_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH` is set
to `False`, since that setting governs a different code path than the
Playwright loader's own redirect-following.

This corpus already carries `observed_open_webui_playwright_subresource_ssrf_t1190`
for a mechanistically DIFFERENT Playwright-related bug (unvalidated
SUB-RESOURCE requests from the loaded page's own JS); this rule is the
simpler, earlier case: an HTTP-level REDIRECT the loader itself follows
without re-checking, no page JavaScript involved.

Detection logic flags a Playwright-loader fetch whose FINAL resolved
URL (after redirects) targets a private, loopback, or link-local
address that DIFFERS from the initially-submitted URL's own address --
a same-target redirect is unremarkable, but a redirect landing on an
internal range the initial validation would itself have blocked is the
exact bypass this advisory describes.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6.
